This is likely with the CLI now piping the `stdio` of the binary in Windows, and is likely not a problem with the binary itself.

The binary ships with its own node version, so whatever one you have locally installed does not affect the binary. However the CLI does run in your own node version, so if by changing the node version it fixes the problem, then that would be the root cause.

Can someone work with the CLI regarding piping stdio and see if they can see the root cause? We are still trying to reproduce on our end to even begin debugging this.

issue.title: cypress: EPIPE error on windows after successful test run
issue.body:
### Version
3.0.0-beta.15

### Reproduction link
[https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windows](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windows)

### Steps to reproduce
- run windows
- create a new repo with cypress tests
- add the following command to package json: "test:e2e:headless": "vue-cli-service test:e2e --headless"
- run the command

### What is expected?
tests pass, process exits

### What is actually happening?
tests pass, EPIPE error

---
Issue with cypress: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/1841
